edits.value_json: 人 is a pictograph of a person in profile. Early examples use it for ‘person’; the whole graph depicts a figure rather than combining separate modern components.

Pictographic: the graph depicts a person in profile. Descriptions interpret its strokes as a head, body, arm and legs; this explains the figure, not a proven stroke-by-stroke sequence. Two early graphic variants are described as equivalent in meaning, with one underlying the Small Seal form and the other developing through clerical writing into regular 人.

Oracle-bone, bronze, Chu-script and Small Seal materials are recorded. The selected oracle-style and seal-script illustrations are modern redrawings of forms in those traditions; they are examples, not evidence of a direct sequence of graphic change.

The Shuowen account describes 人 as depicting an arm and shin, consistent with interpreting the graph as a human figure. A separate account describes two early graphic variants as equivalent in meaning: one underlies the Small Seal form, while the other was common in clerical script and developed into regular 人. Some forms called ancient in later references are not attested in the early corpora checked and should not be treated as established ancestors.
Oracle-bone inscriptions; individual specimen dates unresolved
The graph depicts a person. Cited oracle-bone examples use it in contexts glossed ‘ten people’ and ‘I, the king’; the individual specimens are not dated here.
